source_text:
Εἰδότες, οὖν, ὅτι θεὸς οὐ μυκτηρίζεται, ὀφείλομεν ἀξίως τῆς ἐντολῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ δόξης περιπατεῖν.
ὁμοίως διάκονοι ἄμεμπτοι κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὡς θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ διάκονοι καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπων: μὴ διάβολοι, μὴ δίλογοι, ἀφιλάργυροι, ἐγκρατεῖς περὶ πάντα, εὔσπλαγχνοι, ἐπιμελεῖς, πορευόμενοι κατὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ κυρίου, ὃς ἐγένετο διάκονος πάντων: ᾧ ἐὰν εὐαρεστήσωμεν ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι, ἀποληψόμεθα καὶ τὸν μέλλοντα, καθὼς ὑπέσχετο ἡμῖν ἐγεῖραι ἡμᾶς ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ὅτι ἐὰν πολιτευσώμεθα ἀξίως αὐτοῦ, καὶ συμβασιλεύσομεν αὐτῷ, εἴγε πιστεύομεν.
ὁμοίως καὶ νεώτεροι ἄμεμπτοι ἐν πᾶσιν, πρὸ παντὸς προνοοῦντες ἁγνείας καὶ χαλιναγωγοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ. καλὸν γὰρ τὸ ἀνακόπτεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, ὅτι πᾶσα ἐπιθυμία κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος στρατεύεται, καὶ οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε μαλακοὶ οὔτε ἀρσενοκοῖται βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομήσουσιν, οὔτε οἱ ποιοῦντες τὰ ἄτοπα. διὸ δέον ἀπέχεσθαι ἀπὸ πάντων τούτων, ὑποτασσομένους τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις καὶ διακόνοις ὡς θεῷ καὶ Χριστῷ: τὰς παρθένους ἐν ἀμώμῳ καὶ ἁγνῇ συνειδήσει περιπατεῖν.
orientation: Polycarp is instructing the Philippian church household by household, and now turns from widows to deacons and younger members.
pass_a_gloss: Knowing, therefore, that God is not mocked, we owe [it] worthily of his commandment and glory to walk. Likewise deacons [must be] blameless before him of righteousness, as of God and Christ deacons and not of men: not slanderers, not double-tongued, not lovers of money, self-controlled in all things, compassionate, diligent, walking according to the truth of the Lord, who became deacon of all: to whom if we please in the now age, we shall receive also the coming [age], just as he promised us to raise us from [the] dead, and that if we live as citizens worthily of him, we shall also reign with him, if indeed we believe. Likewise also younger [men must be] blameless in all things, before all things taking thought for purity and bridling themselves from every evil. For good [is] the being cut off from the desires in the world, because every desire against the spirit wages war, and neither fornicators nor soft [men] nor men who lie with males [the] kingdom of God will inherit, nor those doing the improper things. Therefore [it is] necessary to abstain from all these things, submitting to the elders and deacons as to God and Christ: the virgins in blameless and pure conscience [must] walk.

choices.term: ὀφείλομεν ἀξίως τῆς ἐντολῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ δόξης περιπατεῖν
choices.english: we are obligated to walk in a manner worthy of his commandment and his glory
choices.why: Keeps the infinitive 'to walk' as the main obligation and preserves both objects of 'worthy of' (commandment and glory) without smoothing the genitive chain.
rejected: we must walk worthily of his commandment and glory

choices.term: ὡς θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ διάκονοι καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπων
choices.english: since they are deacons of God and Christ, not of human beings
choices.why: The 'as' introduces the ground for blamelessness; rendering it 'since' makes the logic explicit while keeping the contrast with 'not of human beings.'
rejected: as deacons of God and Christ and not of men

choices.why: The demonstrative force of 'now' is best carried by 'present,' and 'age' is the standard rendering for αἰών in this eschatological contrast.

choices.english: if we live as citizens worthily of him
choices.why: The verb πολιτεύομαι carries civic conduct; 'live as citizens' preserves that nuance, and 'worthily of him' keeps the genitive object.
rejected: if we conduct ourselves worthily of him

choices.why: The term is a substantive adjective; 'the soft' keeps the literal force without importing a modern category, leaving the vice list's sense intact.
ἄτοπος means out of place or improper; 'what is improper' keeps the moral force without over-translating as 'lawless' or 'wicked.'

bible_refs.note: οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε μαλακοὶ οὔτε ἀρσενοκοῖται βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομήσουσιν

pass_b_english: Since we know that God is not mocked, we are obligated to walk in a manner worthy of his commandment and his glory.

In the same way, deacons must be blameless before his righteousness, since they are deacons of God and Christ, not of human beings: not slanderers, not double-tongued, not lovers of money, self-controlled in everything, compassionate, diligent, walking according to the truth of the Lord, who became a deacon of all. If we please him in this present age, we will also receive the age to come, just as he promised to raise us from the dead, and if we live as citizens worthily of him, we will also reign with him—if indeed we believe.

In the same way, the younger men must be blameless in everything, concerned above all for purity and bridling themselves from every evil. For it is good to be cut off from the desires in the world, because every desire wages war against the spirit, and neither the sexually immoral nor the soft nor men who lie with males will inherit the kingdom of God, nor those who do what is improper. Therefore it is necessary to abstain from all these things, submitting to the elders and deacons as to God and Christ. The virgins must walk with a blameless and pure conscience.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'love of money' not 'greed' or 'avarice', but 'lovers of money' is not the fixed term.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀφιλάργυροι literally means 'not lovers of money'; rendering is standard and accurate.

last_rejected.why: 'purity' alone misses that ἁγνείας here refers to sexual purity/chastity, especially for young men.
last_rejected.ruling: ἁγνείας means purity/chastity; 'purity' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: 'Soft' is archaic and unclear; μαλακοὶ in this context means effeminate/passive homosexual partners.
last_rejected.ruling: μαλακοὶ literally means 'soft'; rendering is defensible literal translation, not a meaning error.

last_rejected.why: Arsenokoitai is a specific term for active homosexual partners; 'men who lie with males' is vague and inclusive.
last_rejected.fix: men who have sex with men
last_rejected.ruling: ἀρσενοκοῖται etymology supports 'men who lie with males'; within acceptable range.

last_rejected.quote: The virgins must walk with a blameless and pure conscience
last_rejected.source_quote: τὰς παρθένους ἐν ἀμώμῳ καὶ ἁγνῇ συνειδήσει περιπατεῖν
last_rejected.why: Missing 'walk' verb structure; more critically, the subject 'virgins' lacks 'must' or imperative force matching prior clauses.
last_rejected.fix: The virgins must walk in a blameless and pure conscience.
last_rejected.ruling: περιπατεῖν rendered as 'walk'; 'must' supplies imperative force of infinitive. No real omission.

problems.quote: The love of money is the beginning of all troubles
problems.why: Section 2 lists 'greed, love of money' as if distinct; later sections use only 'love of money' for the same vice.
problems.fix: Note that 'greed' and 'love of money' are the same Greek term.

problems.quote: neither the sexually immoral nor the soft nor men who lie with males
problems.why: 'The soft' is a literal rendering of malakoi; modern readers may not recognize it as a vice category.
problems.fix: Translate as 'the self-indulgent' or 'catamites' with a note.

edits.old: neither the sexually immoral nor the soft nor men who lie with males
edits.new: neither the sexually immoral nor the self-indulgent nor men who lie with males

fixed: Glossary problem: 'greed, love of money' in section 2 is not present in this source passage; the source here uses ἀφιλάργυροι, which the English correctly renders 'not lovers of money.' No edit needed.
Mistranslation: μαλακοὶ is rendered 'the soft,' which is literal but unclear in modern English; changed to 'the self-indulgent' to convey the vice category.

problems.why: Same group rendered differently in heading vs body.

edits.old: In the same way, the younger men must be blameless
edits.new: In the same way, young men must be blameless

fixed: Standardized 'the younger men' to 'young men' to match the body rendering, since the source νεώτεροι is the same word in both places.
